messages.author: 8a0adc104fb25fd9
messages.subject: Choice of an appropriate estimator
parts:
Hi all,

I am new to SEM and am estimating my model, which has three independent (exogenous) variables (one of which is ordered into three categories, i.e., 1, 2, and 3), while the other two are continuous. The mediator and the dependent variables (endogenous) are also continous.

I have come across some sources that state that categorical variables can create challenges when employing the traditional Maximum Likelihood approach. 

What remains unclear to me is whether this applies to all categorical variables within the model or specifically to the dependent or endogenous variables. On the other hand, concerning categorical variables, I also found that the "WLSMV" estimator, as provided in lavaan, seems to be the best option.

I would appreciate any recommendations on which estimator I should use. My sample size is 510. I would be grateful if you could share any references with me. 

Thank you for getting back to me.

Richmond

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Choice of an appropriate estimator
parts: (exogenous) variables (one of which is ordered into three categories, i.e., 1, 2, and 3)

If you want to assume linearity, you can just treat it as continuous.  By default (fixed.x=TRUE), no distributional assumption is made about exogenous variables.  To relax the linearity assumption, you can create 2 variables to distinguish between 3 groups (e.g., dummy codes or polynomial contrast codes).
What remains unclear to me is whether this applies to all categorical variables within the model or specifically to the dependent or endogenous variables.
would appreciate any recommendations on which estimator I should use. My sample size is 510.

ML works great (even with robust SEs and test) when your N is that big and only a few observed variables.
